title: Refusing cut-rate offers and the Porgy and Bess stage solo pay dispute
summary: Porgy and Bess producers offered to hire him again at his old salary, and he had earlier bargained from $25 to $75 extra to play Howard Roberts's stage trumpet spot; Delaunay told him to go home rather than work cheaply.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So I could have stayed over much longer, you know, because the show was coming back to Europe, and they wanted somebody that knew the show to play it, and they wouldn't have to worry, you know, about nothing.

And I also knew the part on the stage that Howard Roberts had. You know, he had a trumpet part. He'd go out there and play a little jazz (Singing). Well, I would come out of the pit in the Ziegfield and go up on the stage and do that. And I even made them guys pay me for that, because they come up and said, 'Can you do that?' I said, 'Yeah.' He said, 'Well, okay, we'll give you $25.00 more.' I said, 'Uh-uh. You can get Bill Dillard. He can do that.' I knew they had got to pay him scale, you know. And finally they said, '50.00.' Finally they said, '75.00.' Finally they come up and Cab -- asking Cab, 'Can he go up there and play it?' He said, 'Yeah, there ain't nothing to it. He can do that with his eyes closed.' So I went up on the stage and Cab [said] 'Go on out there and blow that same thing you used to blow.' So I went on up there and did that. So I was getting almost double salary down there, you know. So that's what I wanted over there. So they wouldn't come up on that, so I just come on back home. Come on back, and it was a great thing, you know, 10 weeks there and 4 weeks there, and I enjoyed it and got out before I'd have to go in The Cave and play where they're going to cut you five dollars and the next guy, they're going to cut him five more, and the

next -- uh-uh. So Delaunay had told me everything, you know, that's how come I like him so much. Said, "Don't be going out there and working cheap and everything, because you come over here, you get straight, go on home. That's where so many of them make a mistake. Go home, and then when you come back again, maybe you can get your money again. But if you stay here it's got to go down." I wound up helping some of them guys out over there.
